common_name: Nuccio's Gem Camellia (Formal Double White Camellia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Nuccio's Gem is one of the most widely grown formal double white camellias, valued for its perfectly symmetrical flower form.

directions: Nuccio's Gem, from the renowned Nuccio's Nurseries camellia breeding program in California, is one of the most widely planted formal double white camellias, prized for tightly overlapping, perfectly symmetrical rows of pure white petals that hold their shape exceptionally well from bud to full bloom, making it a favorite among camellia show exhibitors as well as home gardeners. Like other Camellia japonica cultivars it flowers in winter into early spring on a slow-growing, long-lived evergreen shrub with glossy, dark green foliage that provides structure year-round. Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade to filtered light, and protect from harsh afternoon sun and drying wind, which can brown both foliage and the delicate white petals. Prune only lightly right after bloom, since flower buds for the following season set on the current year's growth.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 5.0-6.5), humus-rich soil in partial shade to full sun; a classic, long-cultivated sasanqua valued for its soft, delicate flower color.

directions: Apple Blossom bears single to semi-double flowers in soft white delicately flushed with pink at the petal edges, echoing the blush tones of a spring apple bloom despite flowering in fall and early winter along with the rest of its sasanqua kin. Golden stamens at the flower center provide contrast against the pale petals, and the plant's naturally graceful, spreading habit fits informal borders and woodland-edge plantings as well as a more traditional foundation bed. Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade to full sun — sasanqua camellias generally tolerate more direct sun than japonica types. Prune, if needed, immediately after flowering ends to avoid removing the buds that will open the following fall.

common_name: Cotton Candy Camellia (Semi-Double Clear Pink Camellia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; a popular, widely available camellia valued for its clear, soft pink semi-double flowers and reliable bloom.

directions: Cotton Candy produces large, semi-double flowers in a clear, soft pink with loosely arranged petals surrounding a center of golden stamens, a cheerful, informal flower form that reads as lighter and airier than the tightly formal doubles common in the genus. It blooms over a long midseason window on a vigorous, well-branched evergreen shrub with the glossy dark foliage typical of Camellia japonica, providing structure and interest even when not in flower. Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade to filtered light, and keep soil consistently moist, since camellias struggle in prolonged drought. Prune only right after bloom to shape the plant, since next season's flower buds form on the current year's growth.

common_name: Sparkling Burgundy Camellia (Peony-Form Deep Rose-Red Camellia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; a Camellia japonica-reticulata hybrid grown for its exceptionally large, richly colored peony-form flowers.

directions: Sparkling Burgundy is a Camellia japonica-reticulata hybrid bearing exceptionally large, loosely double, peony-form flowers in a deep rose-red to burgundy-pink, one of the more dramatic, show-quality flower colors and forms available in the genus. It flowers over a long midseason window on a vigorous, upright shrub, and the large flower size and rich color have made it a long-standing favorite among camellia collectors and show exhibitors. Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade to filtered light, protecting the plant from harsh afternoon sun and drying wind, which can damage foliage and shorten flower life. Prune, if needed, right after bloom to keep the plant shapely, since flower buds for the following season form on the current year's growth.
